description: Image normalization: the feature stone's rule lifted over a 4×4×3 image, the per-channel means and spreads broadcast by an index projection, never copied.

line_docs: The array reading, unchanged from the feature stone: subtract the means, divide by the spreads. At rank 3 it is 48 independent scalar rules.

The shapes: the image is a 4×4×3 tuple, the means and spreads are 3-tuples. Their trailing axes agree, so Μ and Σ lift over the image by the index map (h, w, c) ↦ c; the language never materializes a 4×4×3 copy of them.
m.purpose: Line one is the feature-normalization line character for character: the shapes moved from Tuple[3] to Tuple[4,4,3] and the expression did not move at all. Line two declares the shapes; subtracting a Tuple[3] from a Tuple[4,4,3] is broadcasting, an index projection (h, w, c) ↦ c, not a copy. Placeholder glyphs.
m.text:
Z ← (X − Μ) ÷ Σ
X : Tuple[4,4,3] Μ Σ : Tuple[3]
m.title: The feature stone's expression, unchanged, over an image

line_docs: The rule at pixel (h, w), channel c: subtract the mean of channel c, divide by its spread. h and w select the pixel; only c selects the parameters.
The index space: a product of three finite sets, 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 positions, and the rule holds at each of them independently.
math.purpose: Line one is the scalar rule at position (h, w, c): the pixel's channel value, less that channel's mean, over that channel's spread; μ and σ take only c. Line two says where the indices live: three finite sets whose product is the image's 48 positions, each computed on its own.
math.text:
z[h,w,c] = (x[h,w,c] − μ[c]) / σ[c]
h ∈ Fin(4), w ∈ Fin(4), c ∈ Fin(3)
math.title: The rule at one pixel and channel, and the index space

name: image-normalization

docs: The output: the same 4×4×3 shape as the input, every channel of every pixel expressed in units of that channel's spread, zero at its mean.
Open bracket: the indices of an array entry, or the arity of a tuple type.
Close bracket.
Separates indices, and the axes of a shape.
Which row of the image, 0 to 3. The stone's time axis walks the pixels row by row.
Which column of the image, 0 to 3.
Which colour channel: 0 red, 1 green, 2 blue. The only index μ and σ depend on: broadcasting is the map (h, w, c) ↦ c.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
Open parenthesis: group the difference before dividing, or the argument of Fin.
Close parenthesis.
The input: a 4×4 image with three channels, a ramp in each channel plus one bright spot at row 1, column 2, computed by MLPL.
Centre: take the channel's mean away from every pixel of that channel.
The ImageNet channel means 123, 117, 104: three numbers, one per channel, never copied out to the image's 48 positions.
Scale: divide by the channel's spread, so one means one standard deviation. In the notation, ÷.
The standard deviation of each channel: 58, 57, 57. Three numbers, like μ.
The index ranges over the set: it takes each of its values.
Fin(n) is the set of positions 0 to n−1. The image's index space is the product Fin(4) × Fin(4) × Fin(3), 48 positions; the parameters' is Fin(3) alone.
The image's height and its width.
How many channels there are; the arity of μ and σ.
Declares the type of what is on its left.

Tuple[4,4,3] is the image's shape, Tuple[3] the parameters'. X − Μ takes a 3-tuple from a 4×4×3 one: the trailing axes agree, so the language lifts Μ over the image by the index projection (h, w, c) ↦ c and never builds a Tuple[4,4,3] copy of it.

title: Image normalization

visual.purpose: The image as three 4×4 channel grids with the current pixel outlined; μ and σ as three cells each, drawn once, with a leader from the current pixel through its channel's μ and σ to its output cell; the three output grids fill in one pixel per step. The right panel is the index projection that makes the tuples reach every pixel without being copied.
visual.title: Three channel grids in, three out, and the tuples drawn once
